mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 10% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods when UNRATE exceeds 10%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both unemployment rate and payroll employment suggest conflicting labor market signals, which may lead to market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods with simultaneous increases in UNRATE and PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in federal funds rate may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods during a monetary tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods following RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 95 may signal strong supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods when INDPRO exceeds 95, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic expansion, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods with simultaneous GDP and housing starts growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 6%), a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) may signal labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods during a low unemployment regime with declining PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.
